body: Dolly Parton , the extraordinarily versatile singer and songwriter who built up her artistic credibility and commercial fortunes in both country and pop music over more than half a century, died in Nashville on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at the age of 80. Parton had been mostly out of sight eye for the past year following a struggle with unspecified health issues that forced the “9 to 5” singer/songwriter to curtail public appearances and postpone, then cancel her planned 2025 Las Vegas residency. Her death came 17 months after the passing of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, who died on March 3, 2025 at age 82. “At Dolly’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family,” read a press release announcing the awful news. “Dolly’s fans and friends from around the world are encouraged to pay tribute to Dolly on social media by tagging @DollyParton or by leaving a message at www.dollyparton.com. In lieu of flowers the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library at www.imaginationlibrary.com.” Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, shared a message on Instagram after her passing. While not all users appear to be facing this issue, it appears widespread enough for Google to take notice. Meanwhile, a quick look at Google Home settings suggests that access to notes & lists using a voice assistant may have been removed. It feels like we’re reporting on a Google Home bug or a fix almost every other day. Only today, users received some good news following reports of devices refusing to set alarms over voice commands. Sadly, those good times aren’t going to last, and it now looks like yet another function is being impacted by a similar glitch, as some people are seemingly unable to add items to their lists on Google Keep using Google Home voice commands. In a series of complaints on Reddit, including one from Friday, a user claims the voice assistant recognizes their commands perfectly well, but refuses to add items to the list . For instance, if the person asks one of their Google Home devices to “add x to list xyz,” the assistant might respond by saying how many items are on that list, while refusing to add any new items.
